# Testbed for Modules

## Reactive and non-Reactive Inputs

Notice that it is the responsibility of your module server to
assert whichever kinds of inputs it expects.
Consider these [recommendations on server inputs](https://mastering-shiny.org/scaling-modules.html#server-inputs)
on how to do this.

## Inspecting the Reactive Graph

To see the reactive graph of a module,
use the [reactlog](https://rstudio.github.io/reactlog/) package,
as described in
[Mastering Shiny](https://mastering-shiny.org/reactive-graph.html#the-reactlog-package).
Enable it before you run the testbed:

```{r reactlog, eval = FALSE}
reactlog::reactlog_enable()
x_counter_button_app(server_args = list(deep = TRUE))
```

While the app runs, press Ctrl+F3 (Cmd+F3 on macOS)
to show the reactlog up to that point.
Alternatively, after the app stops,
show the reactlog for the complete session:

```{r reactlogShow, eval = FALSE}
shiny::reactlogShow()
```

The testbed displays its inputs and return values,
which adds reactive nodes to the graph.
Inputs and outputs carry their module ID as a prefix:
`test_object-` for your module,
`inputs-` and `returns-` for the testbed's displays.
Other nodes are labelled by their code,
or by their `label` argument, if you give one.
To focus on your module,
search for `test_object` in the reactlog;
it then shows the matching inputs and outputs and their family trees.
See also the section "Changes to the Reactive Graph" in `?module2app`.
